subproblems.title: Leibniz rule for the exterior derivative of a function multiple: d(ψω)(x) = ψ(x)dω(x) + Dψ(x)∧ω(x)
subproblems.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ, every function ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ, every m-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) and every point x ∈ ℝ^P at which ψ and ω are both (Fréchet) differentiable, the m-form ψω : y ↦ ψ(y)·ω(y) satisfies d(ψω)(x) = ψ(x)·dω(x) + alternatizeUncurryFin((Dψ(x)).smulRight(ω(x))). Here d = exteriorDerivative (Mathlib's extDeriv, dη(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dη(x))), Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x, and (Dψ(x)).smulRight(ω(x)) is the continuous linear map h ↦ Dψ(x)(h)·ω(x) from ℝ^P to the m-covectors.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ψ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) (x : Eucl P), DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ x → DifferentiableAt ℝ ω x → exteriorDerivative (fun y => ψ y • ω y : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x = ψ x • exteriorDerivative ω x + ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((fderiv ℝ ψ x).smulRight (ω x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 3 (Leibniz rule; Simon Ch. 6, 4.11: d(γ∘f ω) = γ∘f dω + γ′(f) df∧ω). It is stated pointwise for an arbitrary function ψ and an arbitrary form ω, both differentiable at x.

Setting. P, m ∈ ℕ. ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P), where Λ^m(ℝ^P) = Covector (Eucl P) m is the normed space of continuous alternating m-linear maps (ℝ^P)^m → ℝ. x ∈ ℝ^P is a point at which ψ and ω are differentiable. Write ψω for the m-form y ↦ ψ(y)·ω(y) and D for fderiv ℝ. For a continuous linear functional ℓ on ℝ^P and an m-covector γ, ℓ.smulRight γ is the continuous linear map h ↦ ℓ(h)·γ from ℝ^P to Λ^m(ℝ^P).

1. (Definition of d.) exteriorDerivative is an abbreviation for Mathlib's extDeriv, and extDeriv η x is defined as alternatizeUncurryFin(Dη(x)) for every m-form η and point x. Hence d(ψω)(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(D(ψω)(x)) and dω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(x)).

2. (Product rule.) ψ is real-valued and differentiable at x, and ω is differentiable at x with values in the normed space Λ^m(ℝ^P). The product rule for scalar multiplication (`fderiv_fun_smul`) gives
 D(ψω)(x) = ψ(x)·Dω(x) + (Dψ(x)).smulRight(ω(x)),
 that is, D(ψω)(x)(h) = ψ(x)·Dω(x)(h) + Dψ(x)(h)·ω(x) for every h ∈ ℝ^P.

3. (Linearity of alternatization.) alternatizeUncurryFin is additive (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add`) and commutes with multiplication by the real scalar ψ(x) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul`). Applying it to the identity of step 2 gives
 alternatizeUncurryFin(D(ψω)(x)) = ψ(x)·alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(x)) + alternatizeUncurryFin((Dψ(x)).smulRight(ω(x))).

4. (Conclusion.) By step 1, the left side is d(ψω)(x) and the first summand on the right is ψ(x)·dω(x). Hence d(ψω)(x) = ψ(x)·dω(x) + alternatizeUncurryFin((Dψ(x)).smulRight(ω(x))). ∎
proof_key_steps: By definition, exteriorDerivative = extDeriv = alternatizeUncurryFin ∘ fderiv, so d(ψω)(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(D(ψω)(x)) and dω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(x)).
Additivity and scalar compatibility of alternatizeUncurryFin give d(ψω)(x) = ψ(x)·dω(x) + alternatizeUncurryFin((Dψ(x)).smulRight(ω(x))).

subproblems.title: Multiplication by a C^∞ function maps D^k(U) into D^k(U)
subproblems.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every test form φ ∈ D^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: φ is C^∞, has compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ U) and every C^∞ function ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ, there is a test form η ∈ D^k(U) with η(x) = ψ(x)·φ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (φ : TestFormOn U k) (ψ : Eucl P → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ → ∃ η : TestFormOn U k, ∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x = ψ x • (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2(a)–(d) for the forms η₁ = ψω and η₂ = ψ dω, stated for an arbitrary test form φ ∈ D^k(U). The parent applies it with φ = ω, k = m, and with φ = dω ∈ D^{m+1}(U), k = m + 1.

Setting. P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. φ ∈ D^k(U) = TestFormOn U k means φ : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) is C^∞ (IsSmoothForm, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ∞), has compact support (HasCompactSupport) and satisfies tsupport φ ⊆ U. ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞. For a form g, support g := {x : g(x) ≠ 0} and tsupport g := closure(support g).

1. (Candidate.) Define η : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) by η(x) := ψ(x)·φ(x). An element of TestFormOn U k is a k-form together with proofs that it is C^∞, has compact support and has tsupport contained in U. So it suffices to prove these three properties for η (steps 2–5). The resulting element has underlying form η, so η(x) = ψ(x)·φ(x) holds for every x by definition.

2. (Smoothness.) ψ is C^∞ by hypothesis, and φ is C^∞ because φ ∈ D^k(U). Scalar multiplication ℝ × Λ^k(ℝ^P) → Λ^k(ℝ^P) is continuous bilinear, so x ↦ ψ(x)·φ(x) is C^∞ (`ContDiff.smul`).

3. (Support.) If φ(x) = 0 then η(x) = ψ(x)·0 = 0. Hence support η ⊆ support φ, and taking closures gives tsupport η ⊆ tsupport φ (`tsupport_smul_subset_right`).

4. (Compact support.) φ has compact support, i.e. tsupport φ is compact. By step 3, tsupport η is a closed subset of tsupport φ, hence compact. So η has compact support (`HasCompactSupport.smul_left`, or equivalently `HasCompactSupport.mono` with support η ⊆ support φ).

5. (Support in U.) tsupport η ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ U, by step 3 and the hypothesis φ ∈ D^k(U).

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 2, 4 and 5, η ∈ D^k(U), and η(x) = ψ(x)·φ(x) for every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Define η(x) := ψ(x)·φ(x); it is C^∞ by ContDiff.smul.
φ(x) = 0 implies η(x) = 0, so support η ⊆ support φ and tsupport η ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ U.
η has compact support because φ has; package η as an element of TestFormOn U k, and the formula holds by definition.

subproblems.title: Wedge of a C^∞ 1-form field with a test form: α∧ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U) for ω ∈ D^m(U)
subproblems.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every test form ω ∈ D^m(U) (TestFormOn U m: ω is C^∞, has compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U) and every C^∞ map α : ℝ^P → (ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ) (a smooth field of continuous linear functionals), there is a test form η ∈ D^{m+1}(U) with η(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin((α(x)).smulRight(ω(x))) (that is, η(x) = α(x)∧ω(x)) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : TestFormOn U m) (α : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] ℝ)), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) α → ∃ η : TestFormOn U (m + 1), ∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((α x).smulRight ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2(a), (b), (d) for the form η₃ = Dψ∧ω, stated for an arbitrary C^∞ field α of continuous linear functionals. The parent applies it with α = Dψ = fderiv ℝ ψ, which is C^∞ by `ContDiff.fderiv_right` because ψ is C^∞.

Setting. P, m ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. ω ∈ D^m(U) = TestFormOn U m, i.e. ω is C^∞, has compact support and satisfies tsupport ω ⊆ U. α : ℝ^P → (ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ) is C^∞. For x ∈ ℝ^P, (α(x)).smulRight(ω(x)) is the continuous linear map h ↦ α(x)(h)·ω(x) from ℝ^P to Λ^m(ℝ^P), and alternatizeUncurryFin turns it into an (m+1)-covector. For a form g, support g := {x : g(x) ≠ 0} and tsupport g := closure(support g).

1. (Candidate.) Define η(x) := alternatizeUncurryFin((α(x)).smulRight(ω(x))) ∈ Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^P). An element of TestFormOn U (m+1) is an (m+1)-form together with proofs that it is C^∞, has compact support and has tsupport ⊆ U. So it suffices to prove these three properties (steps 2–4); the pointwise formula then holds by definition.

2. (Smoothness.) α and ω are C^∞. The map (ℓ, γ) ↦ ℓ.smulRight γ from (ℝ^P →L ℝ) × Λ^m(ℝ^P) to (ℝ^P →L Λ^m(ℝ^P)) is continuous bilinear, so x ↦ (α(x)).smulRight(ω(x)) is C^∞ (`ContDiff.smulRight`). alternatizeUncurryFin is the underlying function of the continuous linear map `ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ` (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM_apply`), and continuous linear maps are C^∞ (`ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff`). A composition of C^∞ maps is C^∞ (`ContDiff.comp`), so η is C^∞.

3. (Support.) If ω(x) = 0, then (α(x)).smulRight 0 = 0 (`ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_zero`), and alternatizeUncurryFin(0) = 0 because it is linear (`map_zero` for alternatizeUncurryFinCLM). So η(x) = 0. Hence support η ⊆ support ω.

4. (Compact support and support in U.) By step 3, η has compact support because ω has (`HasCompactSupport.mono`). Taking closures in step 3 (`closure_mono`) gives tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ U.

5. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 4, η ∈ D^{m+1}(U), and η(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin((α(x)).smulRight(ω(x))) for every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Define η(x) := alternatizeUncurryFin((α x).smulRight(ω x)); x ↦ (α x).smulRight(ω x) is C^∞ by ContDiff.smulRight, and composing with the continuous linear map alternatizeUncurryFinCLM keeps it C^∞.
ω(x) = 0 implies (α x).smulRight 0 = 0 and alternatizeUncurryFin 0 = 0, so support η ⊆ support ω.
Hence η has compact support and tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ U; package η as an element of TestFormOn U (m+1).

subproblems.title: Mass estimate from a normalized measure representation: ofReal|T(η)| ≤ ∫⁻ |η| dμ
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), every measure μ on ℝ^P and every v : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) n) such that IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v holds (for every η ∈ D^n(U), x ↦ v(x)(η(x)) is μ-integrable and T(η) = ∫ v(x)(η(x)) dμ(x)) and |v(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(α) for all x ∈ ℝ^P and all n-covectors α: for every test form η ∈ D^n(U), ENNReal.ofReal|T(η)| ≤ ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(covectorEuclideanNorm(η(x))) dμ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n), |v x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → ∀ η : TestFormOn U n, ENNReal.ofReal |T η| ≤ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x)) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 5 (the representation estimate (**)), stated for an arbitrary degree n and an arbitrary test form η. The parent applies it with n = m + 1 and η = η₃.

Setting. P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. T ∈ D_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n, μ is a measure on ℝ^P, and v : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) = NVector (Eucl P) n satisfies IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v: for every η ∈ D^n(U), the function x ↦ v(x)(η(x)) is μ-integrable and T(η) = ∫ v(x)(η(x)) dμ(x). Also |v(x)(α)| ≤ |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm(α) for every x and every n-covector α. Fix η ∈ D^n(U). All inequalities below are in [0,∞].

1. (Representation.) By IsMeasureRepresentation applied to η, T(η) = ∫ v(x)(η(x)) dμ(x).

2. (Absolute value of an integral.) For every real function g on ℝ^P, ‖∫ g dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖g(x)‖ₑ dμ(x) (`enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm`; no integrability hypothesis is needed). For a real number r, ‖r‖ₑ = ofReal|r| (`Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs`). Taking g(x) := v(x)(η(x)) and using step 1:
 ofReal|T(η)| = ofReal|∫ v(x)(η(x)) dμ(x)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|v(x)(η(x))| dμ(x).

3. (Normalization.) For every x, the hypothesis with α := η(x) gives |v(x)(η(x))| ≤ |η(x)|. Since ofReal is monotone (`ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal`), ofReal|v(x)(η(x))| ≤ ofReal(|η(x)|).

4. (Monotonicity of the lower integral.) By step 3 and `lintegral_mono`, ∫⁻ ofReal|v(x)(η(x))| dμ(x) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(|η(x)|) dμ(x).

5. (Conclusion.) Combining steps 2 and 4 gives ofReal|T(η)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(covectorEuclideanNorm(η(x))) dμ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm and Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs give ofReal|T(η)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|v(x)(η(x))| dμ.
The normalization |v(x)(η(x))| ≤ |η(x)| with ofReal monotonicity and lintegral_mono gives the bound ∫⁻ ofReal|η(x)| dμ.
